scenes.line: Share with a parent who needs *this*

caption:
🦟 Dengue fever in children: what every parent should watch, day by day

🌡️ Signs: sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, body & joint pain, rash, vomiting, tiredness

📅 3 phases:
• Fever phase: 2–7 days of high fever
• Critical phase: as the fever comes down (usually day 3–7, lasts 24–48 h)
• Recovery: appetite returns, itchy rash is common
⚠️ Fever going away does NOT mean dengue is over. Days 3–7 need the closest watch.

🏠 At home:
• Paracetamol only, in the dose your doctor advises
• Plenty of fluids: ORS, water, coconut water, soups, juice
• Rest, and blood tests as advised
• Child should pass urine at least every 4–6 hours

🚫 Please don't: give ibuprofen, aspirin or other painkillers · ask for drips/injections without need · rely on home remedies instead of a doctor · relax when the fever stops

🚨 Go to hospital NOW if: belly pain · repeated vomiting · bleeding from gums/nose, black stools, blood in vomit · very sleepy, irritable or restless · cold, clammy hands & feet · no urine for 4–6 hours · fast or difficult breathing

🩸 Platelets: fluid leak (shock) is the real danger, not the platelet number alone. Most children don't need platelet transfusion. Your doctor decides.

🛡️ Prevention: empty & scrub stored water every week · cover tanks · full sleeves in the day · nets & repellents
